purpose: Provide an independently deployable, reproducible, isolated, and resource-governed environment for clean builds, validation, packaging, Software Bill of Materials generation, provenance capture, signing workflows, and production of release candidates for the system, services, governance, and knowledge channels.

conditions: Every release-candidate build starts from a clean worker state.
All source, dependency, toolchain, and configuration inputs are pinned or content-identified.
The build can be repeated from retained inputs and toolchain declarations.
reproducible_clean_builds.degraded_behavior: New release-candidate builds are blocked when clean-worker or reproducibility guarantees cannot be established.
reproducible_clean_builds.rationale: The profile exists to produce repeatable artifacts whose inputs and execution environment can be reconstructed.

conditions: Each worker has a unique workspace identity.
Mutable dependencies, services, ports, data, secrets, temporary files, and process namespaces are isolated.
Concurrent builds cannot modify one another's mutable state.
isolated_parallel_build_workers.degraded_behavior: Concurrency is reduced or new workers are queued; isolation is never weakened.
isolated_parallel_build_workers.rationale: Parallel builds must not create cross-workspace drift or non-reproducible outputs.

conditions: An OCI-compatible runtime is available.
Runtime-specific behavior is used only when explicitly adopted by a toolchain or artifact contract.
Build workers use least privilege and profile-scoped isolation.
oci_build_execution.degraded_behavior: Builds requiring the unavailable runtime are blocked; non-container validation tasks may continue when independently safe.
oci_build_execution.rationale: The build farm requires a portable container execution boundary without making one vendor-specific runtime globally authoritative.

conditions: Kubernetes is deployed only when measured scale or scheduling requirements justify it.
The profile remains conformant without Kubernetes.
Application contracts do not depend on Kubernetes-specific behavior unless explicitly declared.
kubernetes_orchestration.degraded_behavior: Workers use the active non-Kubernetes orchestration path or the affected cluster capability is blocked.
kubernetes_orchestration.rationale: Kubernetes is permitted for the build farm but is not an endpoint or profile baseline requirement.

conditions: Source revisions and dependency lock data are identified before execution.
Untrusted inputs are admitted through declared validation and quarantine controls.
Network retrieval is limited to approved sources or controlled mirrors.
source_and_dependency_admission.degraded_behavior: The farm uses already admitted inputs or blocks builds that require unresolved external inputs.
source_and_dependency_admission.rationale: Reproducibility and supply-chain control require explicit input identity and admission.

conditions: The cache is content-addressed or equivalently integrity-bound.
Cached objects are verified before reuse.
Cache contents do not become authoritative merely because they are available.
artifact_cache.degraded_behavior: Builds continue without cache acceleration when capacity permits; otherwise new work is queued or blocked.
artifact_cache.rationale: The required artifact cache reduces repeated work while preserving input and output integrity.

conditions: Applicable unit, integration, contract, security, reproducibility, and conformance tests run in isolated workers.
Test results are linked to the exact source, toolchain, and candidate artifact identities.
automated_test_execution.degraded_behavior: The candidate remains non-releasable when required tests cannot run or do not pass.
automated_test_execution.rationale: A build artifact cannot become a release candidate without applicable validation.

conditions: Every software artifact class that requires a Software Bill of Materials receives one.
The inventory is bound to the candidate artifact identity and retained with build evidence.
software_bill_of_materials_generation.degraded_behavior: The affected software artifact remains non-publishable until its Software Bill of Materials is generated and validated.
software_bill_of_materials_generation.rationale: Release evidence requires an explicit inventory of software components and dependencies.

conditions: Build provenance identifies source, dependencies, toolchain, worker environment, tests, transformations, and output identities.
A provenance receipt is produced for every published or transferred candidate requiring one.
provenance_and_attestation.degraded_behavior: The candidate may be retained for diagnosis but cannot be published or included in a Release Set.
provenance_and_attestation.rationale: Reproducible builds require machine-readable evidence of how each artifact was produced.

conditions: Signing is required when the artifact class or release policy requires a signature.
Signing keys are isolated from ordinary build workers.
A successful build does not automatically authorize signing.
artifact_signing.degraded_behavior: Unsigned candidates remain staged and non-activatable when a signature is required.
artifact_signing.rationale: Signing is a governed release action separate from compilation and testing.

conditions: Every candidate is classified into the system, services, governance, or knowledge release channel.
Channel metadata and compatibility declarations are produced with the candidate.
release_channel_packaging.degraded_behavior: Unclassified or incompatible candidates remain non-releasable.
release_channel_packaging.rationale: The release model requires explicit channel identity and compatibility.

conditions: Exact candidate versions exist for all required channels.
Cross-channel compatibility tests pass.
The build farm assembles a candidate Release Set but does not activate it in production.
release_set_assembly.degraded_behavior: Individual verified candidates remain available, but no Release Set is emitted.
release_set_assembly.rationale: Release Set assembly binds tested compatible versions without transferring deployment authority to the build farm.

conditions: All required source, dependency, toolchain, trust, and policy inputs are admitted through verified offline bundles or local mirrors.
The sovereign_offline overlay may strengthen this capability.
offline_build_execution.degraded_behavior: Builds requiring unavailable external inputs are blocked; builds with complete admitted inputs continue.
offline_build_execution.rationale: The build farm supports disconnected operation without pretending that missing inputs exist.

conditions: The target architecture is declared by the artifact or release contract.
The selected toolchain and worker support the target architecture.
Architecture-specific tests and evidence are produced.
multi_architecture_builds.degraded_behavior: Unsupported target architectures are blocked without affecting supported architecture builds.
multi_architecture_builds.rationale: The profile supports x86_64 and aarch64 hosts while keeping target-specific behavior explicit.

conditions: The applicable knowledge artifact contract and toolchain are active.
Language packs contain compiled runtime artifacts rather than authoring workspaces.
Runtime packs validate against the target runtime compatibility rules.
knowledge_artifact_builds.degraded_behavior: Affected knowledge-channel builds are blocked; system, services, and governance builds may continue.
knowledge_artifact_builds.rationale: The build farm can produce language and runtime packs without merging authoring and runtime responsibilities.

conditions: SenTient is installed separately from required build services.
Each task is explicitly started and resource-bounded.
Outputs remain candidate inputs and cannot modify release artifacts without normal review and import.
sentient_research_tasks.degraded_behavior: SenTient tasks are unavailable while required build and validation capabilities continue.
sentient_research_tasks.rationale: SenTient may support isolated research but is not part of reproducible build authority.

conditions: No external AI surface participates in required build, test, provenance, signing, packaging, or release-set decisions.
external_ai_assistance.degraded_behavior: No degradation occurs because external AI is not a profile dependency.
external_ai_assistance.rationale: Release candidates must be reproducible and authoritative without an external AI service.

conditions: Only validated candidates and their required evidence are exported.
Transfer preserves artifact identity, provenance, signatures, and release-channel classification.
artifact_export_and_transfer.degraded_behavior: Candidates remain locally staged until an approved transfer path becomes available.
artifact_export_and_transfer.rationale: Build outputs must move to release and deployment authorities without losing integrity or provenance.

conditions: Worker definitions, toolchain locks, admitted inputs, provenance, and retained evidence are sufficient to repeat a build.
Artifact cache loss does not destroy the only copy of authoritative source or release evidence.
rebuild_and_recovery.degraded_behavior: New work is blocked when required recovery inputs are unavailable; verified released artifacts remain unaffected.
rebuild_and_recovery.rationale: The build farm must recover by reconstruction rather than relying on mutable worker state.

conditions: Resource envelopes exist for workers, caches, tests, packaging, signing, and optional heavy tasks.
resource_governor.failure_behavior: New heavy or unconstrained work is blocked; bounded inspection and recovery operations may continue.

conditions: Build workflows use declared task identities and dependency graphs.
Workflow state does not replace artifact provenance or release authority.
orgo.failure_behavior: New workflow scheduling stops; active workers drain or stop according to their task contract.

conditions: The agent coordinates profile state, worker registration, health, and local artifact admission.
koa_node_agent.failure_behavior: Existing safe workers may drain; new node-level activation, registration, or recovery is blocked.

conditions: Worker, source, signer, artifact, and release identities resolve before governed actions.
identity_and_trust.failure_behavior: Identity-dependent admission, signing, publication, and release-set assembly are blocked.

conditions: Critical build, signing, transfer, and release-candidate transitions emit required receipts.
audit_broker.failure_behavior: Transitions requiring durable receipts remain uncommitted; noncritical local diagnostics may continue.

conditions: Required when an active overlay or release policy requires governed authorization, disclosure, consent, exception, or privilege decisions.
governance_policy_runtime.failure_behavior: Governed actions are blocked; Resource Governor does not substitute a policy decision.

conditions: Activated only for language-pack authoring and compilation tasks.
gf_wordbench.failure_behavior: Language-pack builds are blocked; unrelated build channels continue.

conditions: Activated for compatibility and runtime validation of compiled language artifacts.
semantik_architect_runtime.failure_behavior: Language-runtime validation is blocked; the candidate language pack remains non-releasable.

conditions: Isolated research tasks only.
No direct write access to build, source, signing, release, or component-authoritative stores.
sentient.failure_behavior: Only the SenTient task fails or stops; required build capabilities continue.

ai_boundary.fallback_behavior: Required build, test, provenance, packaging, signing, and recovery workflows remain deterministic; optional AI-assisted research is unavailable.
